rv.q: "The Shape of the Bones" is an excellent new play...

If Huffman's play worked purely as a way of anatomizing how cults gain power (and more chillingly, with today's headlines, of how people in power exploit children for their own ends), it would still be highly watchable.

“The Shape of the Bones” as presented here strikes me as a work in progress, a way for the playwright to see his characters in action as he figures out what exactly he has to say about a highly charged, very personal subject.

cn.t: Huffman's religious drama earns praise for devastating performances and gripping direction, though critics are divided on whether the story fully delivers on its promise.
